summary: The smart #1 is a 4.27m electric crossover built on Geely's SEA platform and styled by Mercedes-Benz, sold in Australia by LSH Auto out of just three Mercedes-Benz showrooms in Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane. Australian reviewers consistently rate the driving experience above its price -- a well-damped ride, quick 200kW rear-drive response and a rear seat that slides 15cm and genuinely fits adults -- and it now undercuts a Volvo EX30 on list price. Where opinion turns hostile is the software: nearly every function lives behind a 12.8-inch screen guarded by a fox avatar, and CarExpert singled out the speed-sign warnings and driver-monitoring camera as among the most intrusive it has tested.
pros: Undercuts its SEA-platform sibling the Volvo EX30 (from $49,990) while giving 200kW and 343Nm to the EX30 Plus's 200kW, and undercuts a BMW iX1 by roughly $29,000

150kW DC charging takes 10-80 per cent in under 30 minutes, and the Premium and BRABUS add 22kW three-phase AC -- a real advantage over the Pro+'s 7.4kW single-phase for anyone on a three-phase home supply
Rear bench slides 15cm and folds to 976 litres, so a 4.27m car carries adults in the back with legroom rivals like the Zeekr X cannot match
Rated to tow 1,600kg braked -- the same as an EX30 and unusual for a sub-$50,000 EV of this size
Five-star ANCAP rating, with a heat pump standard on Premium and BRABUS
cons: Climate, mirrors and most vehicle settings are buried in the 12.8-inch touchscreen behind an animated fox avatar; CarExpert found menu navigation deliberately obfuscated and could not reduce the adaptive cruise to plain cruise control

Driver-assist calibration draws repeated complaints: the speed-sign reader misread a 110km/h zone as 70km/h and chimed continuously, and the driver-monitoring camera flagged ordinary glances as distraction

Only three dealerships nationally (Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane) -- there is no smart service point in WA, SA, Tasmania, the ACT or the NT, which also narrows the resale market outside those three cities
Servicing is expensive for an EV: smart's own capped-price schedule runs $1,998 (Pro+) to $2,231 (BRABUS) over five years, with a $666-$701 single visit in years three and four

Residuals are an open question -- list prices were cut about $4,000-$5,000 within two years of the August 2024 launch, on top of near-continuous clearance campaigns, and the brand has no modern Australian resale history to price against
